Subject: Recap: Performance/SLO & concurrency follow-up

Thanks again for your time today — good conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we can size the right option for ACME's pilot.

Key items I captured from the call:
- Primary SLO: p95 latency target for live chat completions <= 200ms.
- Expected peak concurrency: ~1,200 parallel requests (spiky across US region).
- Streaming usage: ~30% of requests use streaming (keep-alive, chunked responses).
- Typical sequence length / tokens: ~80 tokens per completion on average; bursts up to 400 tokens for batch workflows.
- Connection handling: you plan to use connection pooling across app servers with keep-alive; curious whether connection-level concurrency counts vs request-level concurrency.

Questions / asks for ACME to confirm (reply inline):
1) Can you confirm peak concurrent connections vs peak RPS (avg and 95th)?
2) Percent of traffic that is low-latency interactive vs background batch?
3) Any regional split besides US (APAC/EU)?

What we can offer as next steps:
- Temporary hosted quota bump during pilot (30d) to smooth onboarding while we validate traffic patterns.
- Dedicated capacity recommendation (reserve capacity + autoscale) sized to meet p95 and concurrency targets for production.
- If you need strict data residency / audit controls, our Private deployment is an option but adds deployment lead time.

I attached a short QPS summary I put together during the call — if you can fill in peak RPS and percent background traffic that will help us produce a recommendation and quote.

Proposed next meeting: 30-minute tech sync with your infra lead + our infra team to review replay and confirm networking (connection pooling / keep-alive). Are you available Fri 2/27?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Recap: Performance/SLO & concurrency follow-up

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications and numbers from our side:

1) Concurrency / RPS
- Peak concurrent in-production: ~1,200 parallel request contexts across our cluster (this counts live request handlers; streaming connections are long-lived but tracked separately).
- Peak steady RPS observed in last week: ~850 RPS (short spikes to 1.4k RPS for <2 minutes during sales events).

2) Streaming
- ~30% of user-facing chat traffic uses streaming. Streaming connections are long-lived per web-socket or SSE; typically each streaming connection corresponds to 1 active user session.

3) Latency/quality
- Target p95 <= 200ms for interactive chat. Background batch jobs can tolerate p95 up to 2s.

4) Connection pooling
- We use connection pools on app servers (keep-alive). We prefer to keep persistent connections open to reduce TLS overhead; how does Redwood count these vs active request concurrency?

5) Region
- Initial deployment is US-only with potential EU expansion in Q3.

Next steps from us: can you confirm whether Redwood's rate limits are applied per-API-key, per-project, or per-customer? Also interested in a temporary quota bump for the pilot and a ballpark on Dedicated sizing/cost.

Thanks —Jon
Jon Hargreaves
Head of Platform, ACME Corp
jon.hargreaves@acme.com

How Redwood counts concurrency / limits (short version):
- Hosted API: default enforcement is per-customer-project across API keys. We track active request concurrency (requests actively being processed) and streaming connections separately for enforcement.
- Default hosted quotas: 100 RPS and 100 concurrent request handlers per API key (these are defaults for self-serve accounts).
- Streaming default: 50 concurrent streaming connections per API key.

For enterprise accounts we can do the following for a pilot:
1) Temporary hosted quota bump (30d) to cover your pilot spikes: we can increase to 2,000 RPS and 1,500 concurrent request tokens scoped to your project while we validate traffic — requires an MSA addendum and a short security review.
2) Dedicated capacity recommendation: based on 1.2k parallel active requests with ~30% streaming, our preliminary sizing is a small reserved pool with autoscale (equivalent to ~3x production-serving GPUs) to hold steady p95 <200ms for typical seq lengths (80 tokens). We'll produce a costed quote — Laura will draft.
3) Connection counting: connection pooling is fine; we count active requests (requests consuming runtime CPU/GPU) rather than idle keep-alive sockets. Long-lived streaming connections count against the streaming connection quota while they are open.

Action items I propose:
- ACME: share a 24–72h traffic replay or logs (we can sign an NDA for replay if needed).
- Redwood: provide temporary hosted quota bump + short-term rate-limit override for pilot; produce a Dedicated sizing + cost estimate.

I've attached a short PDF summarizing Redwood rate-limit defaults and the proposal for a pilot quota bump. Also linking the HubSpot opportunity for tracking.

Can we book the 30-min replay sync Fri 2/27 at 11am PT? If that works I'll send an invite.
